statement_fidelity.zeta: EXACT classical quasi-RH with explicit 7/8: Mathlib's riemannZeta (comparator imports only Mathlib; no OAI declaration named riemannZeta exists). No extra hypotheses. Mathlib's junk value at s=1 is irrelevant (it is nonzero anyway and the theorem holds at s=1 since riemannZeta 1 = (gamma - log 4pi)/2 != 0, Mathlib lemma riemannZeta_one_ne_zero). Classical claim: zeta(s) != 0 for Re s > 7/8 -- matches.
statement_fidelity.dirichlet: Matches the uniform Dirichlet formulation [FG]; covers all moduli and all (also imprimitive) characters; excluded point only the principal pole. Stronger than the paper's headline for primitive characters (imprimitive L differs by Euler factors nonzero for Re s>0).
statement_fidelity.hecke: Faithfulness rests on challenge-file definitions (theta-product WeakFEPair Lambda times pi^s/Gamma(s), divided by 6). Library lemmas LFunction_eq_ideal_tsum (Re s>1) and LFunction_differentiableAt / entire_nonprincipal (Hecke/IdealBridge.lean) show it is the analytic continuation of sum_I chi(I) N(I)^{-s}; these lemmas are NOT part of the comparator, so a reviewer must check them. Character = MulChar on O/m trivial on units: since Q(sqrt-3) has class number 1 and no real places, this covers all finite-order Hecke characters (analyst reasoning).
statement_fidelity.siegel: Matches the logarithmic Landau-Siegel conjecture (ineffective-looking exists-c form; the paper's argument is effective in principle). Note: it is a trivial corollary of the Dirichlet 7/8 comparator ((1-beta)log q >= (1/8)log 3), but is proved independently.

Q.latex: \begin{theorem}\label{thm:main} Every finite-order Hecke $L$-function over $F=\mathbb Q(\sqrt{-3})$ has no zero in $\Re s>7/8$. The same holds for every Dirichlet $L$-function, including $\zeta(s)$. A pole at $s=1$ for a principal character is allowed. \end{theorem}
Q.paraphrase: A fixed zero-free half-plane Re s>7/8, uniform in character, conductor and height, for all Dirichlet L-functions (incl. zeta) and all finite-order Hecke L-functions of Q(sqrt-3). Resolves the quasi-Riemann hypothesis; excludes Siegel zeros; not RH.

A.latex: Every finite-order Hecke $L$-function over $K$ has no zeros in the half-plane $\Rea s>11/12$. Thus every Dirichlet $L$-function, including $\zeta(s)$, has no zeros for $\Rea s>11/12$.
A.paraphrase: Weaker exponent 11/12 by a different, shorter, non-bootstrap proof.

S.latex: There is an absolute constant $c>0$ such that every real zero $\beta\in(0,1)$ of every primitive nonprincipal real Dirichlet $L$-function of conductor $q\ge3$ satisfies $(1-\beta)\log q\ge c$.
S.paraphrase: No Landau-Siegel zeros (logarithmic form), by an algebraic interpolation-determinant argument.

main_statement.formalized_vs_claimed: Formalized: zeta 7/8, Dirichlet 7/8 (all q, chi), Hecke 7/8 over Q(sqrt-3), Siegel gap (independently). Not formalized: A's separate 11/12 proof, all corollaries (least nonresidue, deterministic square roots, PNT in APs with x^{11/12}log x, Miller test, idoneal numbers, effective class numbers). The Lean 7/8 route apparently skips the paper's 11/12 stage.

Q.claim: Reduce to primitive Hecke characters over F; define beta_*; suppose beta_*>sigma_0. Continuation criterion (Q04): a uniform-in-eta power saving for a probe compared with a Mellin signal containing 1/L^S_F continues 1/L past beta_*, contradiction.
Arithmetic: sextic symbols with zeros kept, prime Gauss identities (gamma_2^3=-alpha), reciprocity phases, smooth calculus, Hecke growth on zero-free disks.
Completed cubic reflection: completed theta sums over cn^3 twisted by sextic symbols reflect to quadratic-twisted dual sums; quadratic large sieve bounds the reflected row energy.
Base probe I_eta(X,Y,Z) (Q16). Low side: separates into additive polynomial x completed theta row; planar additive large sieve + Q13 give I << Z^{1/4+eps} at X=Y=Z^{1/2}.
High side: Poisson in m; rows u a^6; scalar Euler identity: principal row u=1 = nonzero scalar x f_eta (contains 1/L_F); non-principal rows are Hecke twists of the target.
Zero detector: a row with a zero above the floor yields saturated inverse and plain witnesses (Q20); sextic large sieve counts rows (Q21-Q22); everything measured against C(beta_*) (Q25).
Contour analysis, principal extraction, outer rows: margins 1021/25000, 1/40, 1/1200, 43/300, >1; common saving 1/4800 -> Theorem 11/12 with C_I(s)=s-2/3; transfer to Dirichlet.
Part II: assume 7/8<beta_*<=11/12. Compensated probe with prime slots (marked minus rescaled), asymmetric scales X=Z^{17/48}, Y=Z^{23/48}, C_II(s)=s-11/16.
Compensated low estimate via marked reflection, reflected energy and additive Gram bound; local compensation errors.

Two moment inductions: marked inverse moment (Mobius polynomials x prime slots; two Poisson transforms per step, terminal reflected energy) giving eq raw-moment and sixth-power amplification; plain fourth moment with prime factors (excluding inducing characters in Theta; centered cancellation).
Refined row counts from both witnesses; principal normalizer; endpoint inequality; order of choices -> criterion verified at 7/8.

A.claim: Littlewood reduction: A_1(D)<<D^{11/12+eps} for every finite-order nu implies zero-freeness (A06).
Embed A_1 in the sextic family A_u(D) (A03); A_{p^6}=A_1+O(D/Y), so the mean square (A04) with H=D^{1+theta}, Y=H^{1/6} gives 11/12 (A05).
Poisson in u: sextic Gauss sums gamma_{-1} combine with mu into cubic Gauss sums (A07): dual family B_h of cubic-Gauss coefficients; target sum_h |B_h(D)|^2 << D^2.
Realize cubic Gauss coefficients as theta coefficients; complete with cube factors; theta reflection gives quadratic twists chi_h^3; quadratic large sieve gives sum |T_h|^2 << H + H^2/X.
Remove cubes by Mobius inversion; short divisors directly; long divisors via the transfer estimate (two Poisson summations: Gauss -> Mobius -> Gauss) at contracted scales; iterate O(1) times.

S.claim: A real zero with delta=(1-beta)log q small forces primes with chi(p)=-1 to carry almost all of sum log p/p up to X=q^{O(1)}.
Biquadratic field K=Q(sqrt d, sqrt2); points theta_n on a box of side N; three conjugates; interpolation lemma gives a nonzero M x M determinant Delta from monomial rows at degree scale U=N^{4/3}.
Weighted greedy row order alpha_1+H(alpha_2+alpha_3): S_2/S_1 = O(1/H).
For inert p>H, theta^p == sigma(theta) or sigma tau(theta) mod p; unitriangular replacement gives p^{E_p} | Delta, E_p ~ S_1/p.
Compare (1/4)log|N Delta|: lower ~ S_1 log U (inert mass ~ log U by step 1), upper ~ (S_1+S_2)(3/4 log U + ell/2). With H large, N=q^gamma, gamma large, delta->0: 1 <= 7/8, contradiction.
